name: Marswalk Radar — Gale Crater: Pahrump Hills to Hematite Hotspot

crs.local_frame: x = meters East, y = meters North, origin at the SW corner of the bbox

hillshade.source: derived from MRO HiRISE DEM Gale_DEM_SMG_1m
hillshade.derivation: Gaussian smoothing sigma=1.0 px, light azimuth 315, altitude 45

slope.derivation: np.gradient on DEM smoothed with sigma=1.0 px (effective base ~4-6 m)

elevation.units: m (areoid-referenced, negative is normal in Gale)
elevation.derivation: 2x2 block mean of the 2 m DEM

return_time.encoding: uint8, minutes = 2 x value; 255 = not reachable under the slope limit
return_time.derivation: Dijkstra on the reverse graph from the pickup point; same speed model and slope limit as the route

assumptions: Walking speed: Tobler-type hiking curve scaled to 2.5 km/h on flat ground. Exploratory, not validated for suited astronauts on Mars.
Cells steeper than 20 deg are not walkable (hard limit).
20 min at each science stop; EVA budget 6.0 h; crew of 2; pressurized rover pickup at Hematite Hotspot.
Astronaut position in the viewer is simulated along the modelled route (in a real EVA it would come from inertial/visual odometry).
Radiation alert at 3 x the reference rate is illustrative.
Scout robot: drives the modelled route ahead of the crew at 1.0 km/h, assumed for known terrain (Curiosity's top speed is about 0.15 km/h).
warnings: All environmental data are historical observations, not live or forecast values.
RAD values are absorbed dose rates measured by the rover, not human dose (no mSv conversion).
Slope is computed from a 2 m DEM; obstacles smaller than ~4-6 m (single rocks) are not resolved.
HiRISE brightness is NOT used to detect sand: tested on the Bagnold Dunes stops, it does not separate sand from rock.
Curiosity's track is a rover reference, not proof of human traversability.

sources.data: HiRISE DEM Gale_DEM_SMG_1m, HiRISE and CTX mosaics
